summary:
SELENE SCOUT is an interactive 3D lunar landing site navigator and multi-agent mission planning flight deck built for the Artemis generation. Combining live NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data, NASA Moon Trek lunar surface imagery, and a deterministic NumPy orbital and terrain physics engine on a 3D CesiumJS globe, the platform evaluates candidate landing zones across the Lunar South Pole throughout the November–December 2026 mission window.

Users can scrub through a 30-day timeline to track real-time 3D Sun and Earth sightline vectors, compare key Artemis candidate sites including Shackleton Crater Rim, Connecting Ridge, and Malapert Massif, or launch an autonomous 48-zone AI terrain scan. A natural-language command bar and a three-agent Gemini Mission Control Council translate deterministic physics telemetry into clear engineering trade-offs across solar power survival, Direct-to-Earth communications, and lander slope safety.

At the Lunar South Pole, shifting a landing site by just 200 meters can separate near-continuous sunlight from fatal cryogenic darkness. SELENE SCOUT bridges complex orbital mechanics and public accessibility replacing static, fragmented spreadsheets with an intuitive spatial tool that empowers both mission planners and students to evaluate lunar landing feasibility in seconds.
details:
What SELENE SCOUT Does & How It Works

SELENE SCOUT (https://selene-scout-kpyt6jazya-as.a.run.app/)is an interactive 3D lunar landing site navigator and multi-agent mission planning flight deck built for the Lunar South Pole (85°S–90°S) across the November 15 – December 15, 2026 Artemis mission window.

The system pairs a deterministic orbital and terrain physics engine with a tiered Google Gemini AI layer on top of an interactive 3D CesiumJS lunar globe:

1. Live NASA Data Ingestion: At startup, the backend concurrently queries the NASA JPL Horizons API to retrieve topocentric Sun and Earth ephemeris vectors and optical libration across 720 hourly timesteps (with an analytical USNO fallback), while the 3D globe streams live NASA Moon Trek WMTS surface imagery (LRO WAC Mosaic 303 ppd).

2. Deterministic Physics & Horizon Ray-Marching: Using a 200×200 polar stereographic elevation model calibrated to NASA LRO LOLA topography, a NumPy physics engine ray-marches 72 azimuth angles per coordinate to compute true local terrain horizons, solar illumination fraction, longest continuous darkness, Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication availability (>3° clearance), maximum blackout duration, and central-difference terrain slope.

3. Interactive 3D Exploration & Autonomous Scouting: Users can inspect all five NASA ESMD candidate sites (Connecting Ridge, Malapert Massif, Shackleton Crater Rim, de Gerlache Rim, and Shackleton Crater Floor as a Permanently Shadowed Region contrast case), scrub a 30-day orbital timeline at 1×/100×/1000× speeds to observe real-time 3D Sun and Earth sightline vectors, trigger an autonomous 48-point polar grid scan, or issue natural-language commands to fly across sites.

Benefits & Intended Impact

At the Lunar South Pole, low-angle sunlight creates extreme micro-topographic trade-offs where a 200-meter shift separates prolonged solar power from fatal cryogenic darkness inside a crater. Traditional mission analysis relies on fragmented 2D plots and offline scripts that are slow to compare and inaccessible to non-specialists. SELENE SCOUT unifies power, communications, and slope constraints into a single real-time spatial interface allowing mission planners to screen landing tradeoffs in seconds while giving educators, students, and the public an intuitive, visual way to understand why Artemis landing site selection is so challenging.

Tools, Languages & Software Stack

- Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, CesiumJS (WebGL 3D planetary rendering), Zustand (state management), Tailwind CSS, and Vite.

- Backend & Physics Engine: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, and NumPy.

- Generative AI & Cloud Infrastructure: Google Gemini API via Vertex AI (gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.7-flash, and gemini-3.8-flash), containerized with Docker and deployed on Google Cloud Run (asia-southeast1).

- Open-Source Repository: https://github.com/sohailrqureshi/nasa-space-challenge-2026

Creativity & Engineering Design Factors

- Strict Separation of Physics and AI: Language models never compute orbital angles, solar fractions, or slopes. All numerical metrics come from deterministic NumPy code, while Gemini receives verified telemetry as ground-truth facts.

- Multi-Agent Systems Engineering Synthesis: Rather than merely paraphrasing dashboard numbers, three concurrent Mission Control Council agents stream domain-specific engineering consequences over Server-Sent Events (SSE): the Power Officer sizes battery reserves against a 200 W survival heater load and 50 kWh budget. the Comms Officer evaluates 2 Mbps downlink deficits against an 8-hour critical-phase limit and the Flight Director assesses the 15° lander tip-over threshold to issue a Go/Caution/No-Go verdict.

- Polar Math & Latency Optimization: To prevent the 60× longitude distortion and acos azimuth singularities that occur near 89°S, all terrain ray-marching runs in polar stereographic projection using atan2 spherical trigonometry. To keep UI interactions instantaneous, model thinking budgets are tiered: 0 on gemini-3.5-flash-lite (<500 ms TTFT for camera commands), 512 on gemini-3.7-flash (concurrent council streaming), and 8,192 on gemini-3.8-flash (batch 48-zone ranking).

- Accessibility & Compliance: Packaged as a zero-setup live web app with one-click demo presets, an in-app Super Intelligence (SI) transparency notice, and strict adherence to NASA brand guidelines (no NASA logos, insignias, or agency flags).
